headline: Light rain arrives Saturday afternoon and night, tapers Sunday morning, then cool, cloudy, mostly dry weather follows through next week.
summary: As of Friday evening, skies are mostly clear but will turn mostly cloudy overnight as a low-pressure system approaches from British Columbia. Overnight lows should reach the mid 30s in the Cascades and nearby foothills and the low 40s around Puget Sound. Rain begins along the coast Saturday afternoon and spreads inland Saturday night into Sunday morning, falling mostly on the Olympic Peninsula and west of the Cascades. Totals will vary a lot: the coast and the windward (wet-side) slopes of the Olympics could get up to three quarters of an inch, while the Puget Sound area should see only a few hundredths to a tenth of an inch. Showers taper off late Sunday morning, leaving cloudy skies and highs in the mid to upper 50s. Next week looks cool and cloudy, with the low staying offshore through midweek. A weak disturbance gives a slight chance of light rain from Tuesday afternoon through late Tuesday night, with no more than a few hundredths of an inch expected. Wednesday through Friday look drier as the system moves inland, with highs staying in the mid to upper 50s all week. Forecasters are also watching a possibly more active pattern from October 31 to November 6, but it is far off and uncertain, with only a 20-40% chance of heavier rain, stronger winds and possibly mountain snow. Forecasters say models now agree more on early next week, which raises confidence in the cool, cloudy outlook. No watches, warnings, or advisories are in effect.
changes: Earlier discussions had a lingering rain chance into Monday and a growing chance of below-freezing overnight lows midweek. The evening update instead has rain ending Sunday morning, a slight chance of light rain Tuesday, and no mention of freezing lows, with highs in the mid to upper 50s all week. It also added specific rain totals and a far-off look at October 31 to November 6, and the Small Craft Advisories had expired.
